name: Marc Berman
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Business and Professions Committee
district: California State Assembly District 23 (southern San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County, including Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Mountain View, Los Altos, Campbell, Saratoga; represented as District 24 from 2016–2022 before redistricting)
years_of_service: First elected November 2016, sworn in December 2016; currently serving his fifth term (District 24, December 2016–2022; District 23, 2022–present). Re-elected in June 2/November 2026 primary and general elections cycle is not yet complete as of this profile's last-updated date. (Source: official Assembly biography, a23.asmdc.org; Ballotpedia.)
background: Berman was born October 31, 1980, in Dallas, Texas, and raised in Palo Alto, California, where he attended Palo Alto High School and served as student body president. He earned a B.A. in Political Science from Georgetown University in 2002 and a J.D. from the USC Gould School of Law, where he was president of the Student Bar Association and a member of the Southern California Law Review. During and after college he worked in Rep. Anna Eshoo's district office, as an analyst in the U.S. Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division, and later at the Truman National Security Project and the Silicon Valley Education Foundation on STEM-education initiatives. (Source: Ballotpedia, Marc Berman; official Assembly biography.)

Before running for the Legislature, Berman practiced law as an attorney at Merino Yebri, LLP and at Latham & Watkins LLP, where he did pro bono work representing clients seeking protection under the Violence Against Women Act and individuals seeking asylum from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. He served on the Palo Alto City Council, focusing on infrastructure and financial transparency, before his election to the Assembly. (Source: official Assembly biography; Wikipedia, Marc Berman.)

Berman was first elected to the Assembly in November 2016, winning an open Democrat-vs-Democrat general election against fellow Democrat Vicki Veenker 54.4%–45.6% for the open District 24 seat. He was re-elected in 2018 (76.6%, vs. Republican Alex Glew), 2020 (73.4%, vs. Republican Peter Ohtaki), and, after 2021 redistricting moved his seat to District 23, in 2022 (73.4%, vs. Republican Tim Dec) and 2024 (59.8%, vs. fellow Democrat Lydia Kou). He chairs the Assembly Business and Professions Committee and previously chaired the Assembly Elections Committee for his first five years in office; the Assembly's official count credits him with sending 107 bills to the Governor in his first nine years in office, 103 of which were signed into law. (Source: Ballotpedia, Marc Berman; official Assembly biography.)
committee_memberships: Chair, Assembly Business and Professions Committee
Member, Assembly Elections Committee (chaired this committee for his first five years in office)
Chair, Assembly Select Committee on the Master Plan for Higher Education in California
voting_record_highlights: AB 2839 (2023–2024), restricting the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated ('deepfake') content about candidates and election matters close to an election: Berman was a lead author with Asm. Gail Pellerin. It passed the Assembly concurrence vote on Senate amendments 63–8 on August 30, 2024, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on September 17, 2024 as Chapter 262, Statutes of 2024. A federal judge in the Eastern District of California (Kohls v. Bonta) issued a preliminary injunction on October 2, 2024, and later a permanent injunction (August 2025), blocking enforcement of the law's disclaimer/takedown provisions on First Amendment grounds; California has appealed to the Ninth Circuit. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2839; web search summary of Kohls v. Bonta rulings — not independently verified against a single primary court-record URL in this session.)

AB 2584 (2021–2022), reforming recall-election procedures (raising signature-verification requirements, allowing public inspection of petitions during the review period, and permitting recall elections to be consolidated with regularly scheduled elections within 180 days): Berman was the lead author. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 59–15, and it was signed by Gov. Newsom on September 29, 2022 as Chapter 791, Statutes of 2022. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2584.)

SB 42 (2025–2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Berman is listed as a Principal Assembly coauthor (alongside other Assembly and Senate principal coauthors including Becker, Blakespear, Kalra, Lee, and Pellerin, with Umberg, Allen, and Cervantes as lead authors). The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29–8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Berman was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records located are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. A CalMatters Digital Democracy legislator profile page was sought during research for this file but returned a 404/not-found error in this session, so it could not be checked as a supplementary source.
